mentl/b2cfb6c:
The deepest generative leap, and the AST-in-graph fabric is exactly what it
needed. Every program node is a resolvable handle, so equality saturation is
a cursor read over the one graph — no e-class machinery beyond a directed
union-find pointed at the cheaper node (the root IS the extracted term, so
there is no separate extraction pass).

The ultimate-medium edge no other e-graph has: rewrites are EFFECT-GATED. egg
rewrites syntactically; Mentl reads each operand's purity from the resolved
program (is_pure — conservative: a literal/var is pure, a call may perform
effects) and fires a DROPPING rewrite (x * 0 ≡ 0) only when the dropped
operand is provably pure. Proof, not heuristic — preserving what RUNS, not
only what the value equals.

src/egraph.mn: the EGraph effect (egraph_rewrite / egraph_extract), the
egraph_ledger handler (the relation as swappable state — a cost model or a
proof-carrying extractor swaps in with no rule change), is_pure (the gate),
the identity (x+0, x*1) and absorbing (x*0) rewrite rules, and saturate
(apply-to-fixpoint). Gate-green (seed builds, micros pass, census 179).

The engine reads the graph-resident AST live. Wiring it into lower's read
path (lower extracts each node's canonical handle before emitting) adds
EGraph to the lowering row right next to the evidence seam PLAN §7 calls
acutely fragile to any row delta — so that integration is deliberate and
WAT-verified, the next move on this branch.

mentl/b2ba4f7:
The form that best translates intent into computation. Articulates
Inka's IDEAL syntax under dream-code discipline, not constrained
by current parser behavior.

Authority: this document binds the parser. Where another doc
conflicts, SYNTAX.md is correct. Ω.4's parser refactor implements
this exactly.

Decisions frozen:
• Function body discipline — single-expression vs block;
  E_RedundantBraces for braces-around-single-expression
• `><` as structural N-ary — parenthesized pipelines on
  each side, indented-center on own line; E_LayoutViolation
  for any deviation
• Record literal {name: "M", age: 30} — colon-binding,
  field punning, alphabetical sort at parse, structural type
• Record type {name: String, age: Int} — inline structural,
  row polymorphism via ...R, optional nominal wrap via type
• Handler declarations — config params (closure capture) +
  state (with clauses) + arms
• Effect declarations — parameterized as first-class;
  Sample(44100) and Sample(48000) are distinct in row algebra
• Lambdas — fn (params) => expr, single-expression body
• Pipeline layout — sequential at left edge, convergent at
  indented center, return-to-left after convergent; `~>`
  newline-sensitive (block vs inline)
• Comments — // line, /// doc; no block comments
• Imports — import path/to/module; selective {names}; no rename
• Strings — ".." with escapes, "hello, ${name}" interp,
  triple-quote multi-line
• Operator precedence — one canonical table; block-form ~>
  at lowest (wraps chain), inline at middle, |> at high
• Pattern syntax — PVar / PWild / PLit / PCon / PTuple /
  PList (with ...rest) / PRecord (with field punning + ...rest)
• Generic type params — angle brackets at decl, inferred at
  call; no turbofish
• Refinement types — type Sample = Float where ...self...
  with Verify discharging the Predicate
• Top-level program structure — import / type / effect /
  handler / fn / let
